summary:
This bill would cancel a rule from the Department of Education about federal student loans.

The rule is called “Waivers and Modifications of Federal Student Loans.” It includes the one-time federal student loan debt relief plan announced on a government website. It also includes a notice printed in the Federal Register on October 12, 2022. The Federal Register is where the government publishes official rules and notices.

The bill uses a law called the Congressional Review Act. This law lets Congress review and cancel rules made by federal agencies.

If this bill becomes law, Congress would disapprove the Education Department’s student loan rule. The rule would have “no force or effect.” That means it could not be used or enforced.

The bill also mentions a March 17, 2023, letter from the Government Accountability Office. That office said the student loan changes count as a rule under the Congressional Review Act.

The House of Representatives passed this bill on May 24, 2023. It was received by the Senate on May 30, 2023.
